question: Q4 alternatives: other ways to compute this quarter-step (rotation by 16 in fewer ops; other add trees)
number: no 4-op program computes the lane-wise ror16 (clean 32-bit result, arbitrary 36-bit lane input incl. guard garbage, arbitrary neighbour lanes) in family A (66 unary ops: shifts and interval/complement masks; 428984831 nodes tried, 0 found) nor in family B (all 35 shift amounts, 92 unary ops, 1831252273 nodes, 0 found). The same search finds the shipped 5-op form (shr, shl, and, and, or/xor/add; 72 variants) in a small validation family, so it can see such programs. Add alternatives: 3 equal-cost trees, none cheaper. The rotation part stays 5 ops and the step stays 8 ops.
notes: Family-limited: shl/shr by the listed amounts, and with lane-replicated interval masks and their complements, reg-reg and/or/xor/add; no xor/add immediates; the middle lane of a 3-lane model must be exact. Outside the family this is OPEN.
held_fixed: Held fixed: the shipped 595-op circuit (research/blake3_r3/candidate_blake3/experiments/rho.py: 7 lanes x 36 bits, ops add/and/or/xor/shl/shr, constants folded) re-derived by our own tracer b3core.py (595 ops; equals the scalar 3-round digest on 300+ batches; scalar core equals verifier/blake3.py on 3 and 7 rounds and the official 7-round fixture). Rotation by 16 with inputs allowed to carry guard bits (xor of an unclean sum).
reopen_if: a 4-op rotation using xor/add immediates, other shift sets, or a lane pitch other than 36
